source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
On my Linux machine, most components were missing from the 3D viewer when I opened the integrated board. The project contained several absolute Windows paths and references to local libraries that I don't have, so I repaired them on my side.

For example, there were 24 hard-coded Windows paths under a private Upwork workspace, ending in libs/componentvault/componentvault.3dshapes/...; I changed them to the relative form ${KIPRJMOD}/libs/componentvault/componentvault.3dshapes/.... The files are already in libs/, so the references now work across machines.

Making this correction is not a problem for me; I only wanted to let you know.

value_updates.project_asset_reference_policy: Use project-relative ${KIPRJMOD}/libs/... references instead of machine-specific absolute paths.
value_updates.cross_machine_compatibility: Project 3D-model references must resolve across machines rather than depending on the designer's local Windows environment.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text: The variable ${KICAD8\_3RD\_PARTY} belongs to KiCad 8, whereas KiCad 9 uses ${KICAD9\_3RD\_PARTY}. Consequently, references to the former would fail under KiCad 9 even on a machine with the JLCPCB plugin installed.

value_updates.kicad_9_third_party_reference_policy: Use ${KICAD9\_3RD\_PARTY} for third-party library references under KiCad 9; ${KICAD8\_3RD\_PARTY} is not compatible with KiCad 9.

routing_warnings.description: The request for three missing 3D-model files primarily concerns bundling project assets; the later message 934 provides the more direct evidence for portable reference paths.
The statement that every library should have been included concerns missing bundled project assets rather than the portability of their reference paths.
The USBLC6 library defect incorrectly joining GND and VBUS is an electrical USB-protection issue, not a KiCad path-portability issue.
